papers.title: Technology and Intelligence: Staying on Target for the Next Decade of Electrophysiology.
Nuclear magnetic resonance therapy for deep-tissue biophysical stimulation: an integrated clinical and molecular analysis.
papers.abstract: Musculoskeletal disorders such as osteoarthritis, chronic low back pain, radicular syndromes, and osteoporosis require noninvasive treatments reaching deep anatomical structures. Nuclear magnetic resonance therapy (NMRT/MBST) delivers depth-independent resonance-based stimulation. This systematic review consolidates clinical and mechanistic evidence to evaluate NMRT/MBST among deep-tissue biophysical therapeutics. A systematic search of PubMed, Ovid/Embase, and peer-reviewed literature identified 26 original studies spanning randomized and observational clinical evidence, imaging evaluations, veterinary trials, and in vitro research. Experimental findings on inflammatory, metabolic, mitochondrial, redox, and circadian pathways were integrated with clinical observations. NMRT/MBST shows a strong safety profile with no reported treatment-emergent adverse events. Across indications, studies demonstrate improvements in pain, function, and, selectively, structural or densitometric changes. Mechanistic evidence indicates modulation of mitochondrial bioenergetics, redox balance, inflammatory cascades, chondrogenic and osteogenic pathways, neurotrophic activity, and circadian regulation. These convergent processes mirror photobiomodulation, supporting NMRT/MBST as a deep-acting analog influencing regenerative biology in inaccessible tissues. Conventional pulsed electromagnetic field therapy is physically the closest comparator but shows narrower mechanistic overlap. Evidence remains heterogeneous in methodology, outcome measures, and structural responses. The only placebo-controlled knee osteoarthritis trial found no superiority over sham, although baseline imbalance limits interpretation. The depth-independent profile and mechanistic parallels suggest applications in deep cartilage, subchondral bone, intervertebral discs, and nerve-root environments, supporting multimodal biophysical strategies. Priorities include larger randomized trials, longitudinal structural evaluation, comparisons with optical modalities, and biomarker-guided personalization.

papers.title: Deep Sedation in Single-Shot Pulmonary Vein Isolation: A Head-to-Head Look at Two Pulsed Field Versus Cryoballoon Ablation Approaches.
papers.abstract: Deep sedation (DS) is routinely used during single-shot pulmonary vein isolation (PVI) to optimize patient comfort and procedural stability. However, data on sedative requirements and procedural tolerance of pulsed field ablation (PFA) under DS compared with thermal technologies remain limited. In this single-center study, consecutive patients underwent PVI with cryoballoon (CB), PFA using a pentaspline catheter (PC) or the balloon-in-basket catheter (BC). All procedures were performed under DS with midazolam, fentanyl, and propofol, administered by electrophysiology staff without anaesthesiologist supervision. Propensity score matching (1:1:1) was applied for age, sex, body mass index, and hypertension. Procedural characteristics, sedative/analgesic requirements, and complications were analyzed. Acute PVI without major complications was achieved in all 156 enrolled patients. PC procedures were associated with higher body-weight- and time-adjusted requirements for propofol (CB: 0.10 ± 0.04 mg/kg/min; PC: 0.15 ± 0.04 mg/kg/min; BC: 0.11 ± 0.03 mg/kg/min; p < 0.001) despite the lowest total dose of propofol used (CB: 440 ± 144 mg; PC: 348± 80 mg; BC: 433 ± 160 mg; p = 0.00). Procedural times (CB: 47.5 [40-60] min, PC: 29 [25-35] min, BC: 47.5 [40-56] min, p < 0.001) and fluoroscopy times (CB: 9.5 [6.3-13.6] min; PC: 6.2 [4.4-9] min; BC: 7.2 [6.1-11.2] min, p = 0.001) were shortest in the PC group. Sedation-related hemodynamic stability was comparable across all cohorts. The novel BC demonstrated excellent feasibility under DS, with reduced normalized sedative requirements compared with the PC and a safety profile comparable to CB ablation. These findings suggest that optimized waveform design and field homogeneity may enable safe and comfortable PVI under DS without the need for general anesthesia.

papers.title: Advanced Two-Stage Authentication with EEG: Inter-Subject P300 ERP Classification Using EEGNet for User Recognition.
papers.abstract: A reliable biometric system is crucial in modern security challenges. EEG signals offer a promising alternative to conventional biometrics due to their uniqueness, forgery resistance, and long-term stability. Among EEG-based approaches, P300 event-related potentials (ERPs) are widely studied for their robustness in distinguishing individuals. This study proposes a two-stage authentication framework integrating user identification (multi-class classification) and authentication (binary classification) for enhanced security. A comprehensive EEG preprocessing pipeline including bandpass filtering, epoch rejection, temporal cropping, and downsampling was implemented to improve signal quality and extract cleaner P300 responses. EEGNet, a lightweight convolutional neural network designed for EEG analysis, was used for feature extraction and classification. 16 participants across three sessions evaluated the system robustness under cross-session conditions. The framework demonstrated strong generalization, achieving up to 95% precision and a mean accuracy of 96.10% for both identification and authentication. These results highlight the potential of EEGNet user authentication using P300 ERPs, offering insights into optimal preprocessing and deep learning methods for EEG-based security. This study underscores brainwave-driven authentication as a secure and viable alternative to traditional biometrics, paving the way for real-time applications in cybersecurity and identity verification.

papers.title: Comparison of quality of life between docetaxel and weekly paclitaxel in the neoadjuvant or adjuvant treatment of breast cancer.
papers.abstract: Taxane-based chemotherapy remains a cornerstone of neoadjuvant and adjuvant treatment for stage II-III breast cancer. Weekly paclitaxel and 3-weekly docetaxel exhibit comparable oncologic efficacy but differ in toxicity profiles and treatment schedules. This study aimed to compare longitudinal patient-reported quality-of-life (QoL) outcomes between these two taxane regimens. This single-center observational cohort study included 82 patients with stage II-III breast cancer who received anthracycline-based chemotherapy followed by either docetaxel every 3 weeks (n=55) or weekly paclitaxel (n=27). QoL was assessed at four time points using the Functional Assessment of Cancer Therapy-Breast (FACT-B), Beck Anxiety Inventory, Beck Depression Inventory, Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index, and Quality of Life Enjoyment and Satisfaction Questionnaire. Longitudinal changes and between-group differences were also analyzed. Baseline QoL scores were comparable between groups. During active treatment, both regimens were associated with deterioration in several QoL domains, with recovery observed following treatment completion. At the third assessment time point, corresponding to peak treatment burden, patients receiving docetaxel reported significantly higher depressive symptoms and lower life satisfaction compared with those receiving weekly paclitaxel. However, global FACT-B scores or sleep quality showed no significant differences at any time point. Hematologic adverse events, particularly anemia and neutropenia, were more frequent in the docetaxel group, whereas peripheral sensory neuropathy was more common with weekly paclitaxel. No grade 4 adverse events or treatment-related deaths occurred. Weekly paclitaxel and 3-weekly docetaxel yielded broadly comparable longitudinal QoL outcomes in curative-intent breast cancer treatment. Docetaxel was associated with a greater short-term psychological burden during peak chemotherapy exposure. These findings highlight the importance of incorporating patient-reported outcomes into treatment selection and supportive care strategies.

papers.title: Psychiatric symptoms were not associated with obstructive sleep apnea severity in a Japanese working population.
papers.abstract: To evaluate the association between obstructive sleep apnea (OSA) severity and psychiatric symptoms, including depression, anxiety, insomnia, and excessive daytime sleepiness, and quality of life, in a Japanese working population. We conducted a cross-sectional study of 707 municipal employees in Japan who participated in the Night in Japan Home Sleep Monitoring study. OSA severity was assessed using the respiratory event index (REI) obtained from home sleep apnea testing and categorized as none, mild, and moderate-to-severe. Psychiatric symptoms were evaluated using validated questionnaires: the Patient Health Questionnaire-9, Generalized Anxiety Disorder-7, Athens Insomnia Scale, and Japanese version of Epworth Sleepiness Scale. Multivariable logistic regression analyses adjusted for demographic, lifestyle, and occupational factors. Sensitivity and subgroup analyses were performed. Among the 707 participants (mean age 44.8 years ± 11.5 years; 58.0% female), 263 (37.2%) had OSA, including 171 (24.2%) with mild OSA and 92 (13.0%) with moderate-to-severe OSA. After adjustment, OSA severity was not associated with insomnia, depression, anxiety, or excessive daytime sleepiness. No significant differences in quality-of-life scores were observed across OSA severity groups. In this working population, objectively measured OSA severity was not significantly associated with most psychiatric symptoms or quality of life. These findings suggest that OSA severity alone may not adequately reflect the aspects of sleep disturbance most relevant to mental health in this Japanese working population. UMIN-CTR (UMIN000028675, August 15, 2017) and ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT03276585, August 3, 2017).

papers.title: Effects of Transcranial Direct Current Stimulation on Core Symptoms and Sleep Disturbances in Children With Autism Spectrum Disorder: A Meta-Analysis of Randomized Controlled Trials.
papers.abstract: This meta-analysis was designed to determine whether transcranial direct current stimulation (tDCS) confers measurable benefits for selected behavioral features of autism spectrum disorder (ASD) and for sleep problems in pediatric ASD populations. A comprehensive literature retrieval was conducted across eight electronic databases-PubMed, Cochrane Library, Web of Science, Embase, CNKI, CBM, VIP, and Wanfang-covering the period from each database's inception through June 1, 2026. Eligible studies were randomized controlled trials (RCTs) that evaluated the therapeutic efficacy of transcranial direct current stimulation (tDCS) in patients with autism spectrum disorder (ASD). The methodological quality of the included trials was appraised using the Cochrane Risk of Bias assessment instrument. Quantitative synthesis was performed with RevMan 5.4 and Stata 17.0, following the PRISMA statement for systematic reviews and meta-analyses. Ultimately, seven studies qualified for inclusion in this systematic review. Pooled analyses showed that tDCS was associated with lower ATEC scores (mean difference [MD] = -8.81, 95% confidence interval [CI]: -12.06 to -5.56, p < 0.00001), ABC scores (MD = -12.08, 95% CI: -21.75 to -2.41, p = 0.01), and CSHQ scores (MD = -4.95, 95% CI: -8.66 to -1.24, p = 0.009). However, no statistically significant difference was observed for CARS scores (MD = -1.12, 95% CI: -4.15 to 1.91, p = 0.47). tDCS, most commonly delivered at 1 mA over the DLPFC, was associated with improvements in some ASD-related behavioral outcomes; preliminary evidence also suggested a potential benefit for sleep disturbances, although this finding was based on only two low-certainty studies and warrants cautious interpretation.

papers.title: Orforglipron for Obstructive Sleep Apnea: Research Summary.
Orforglipron for Obstructive Sleep Apnea: Results From 2 Randomized Clinical Trials (ATTAIN-OSA).
papers.abstract: Obstructive sleep apnea (OSA) is a common disorder characterized by repeated upper airway collapse during sleep that is associated with reduced quality of life and increased incidence of cardiometabolic disease. To assess the effects of orforglipron on moderate to severe OSA in adults with obesity or overweight, compared with placebo. Two 52-week, phase 3, multicenter, double-blind, placebo-controlled randomized clinical trials were conducted at 66 sites in the US, Argentina, Brazil, China, Czech Republic, Germany, Japan, Mexico, and Taiwan. Adults with moderate to severe OSA and body mass index (BMI; calculated as weight in kilograms divided by height in meters squared) of 27 or higher were enrolled between November 11, 2024, and July 23, 2025. Final follow-up occurred on July 30, 2026. Trial 1 included patients not receiving positive airway pressure treatment and trial 2 included patients receiving positive airway pressure treatment. Patients were randomized (1:1) to receive either once-daily orforglipron (maximum tolerated dose: equivalent to 9-, 14.5-, or 17.2-mg tablet dose) or placebo. The primary end point was change in apnea-hypopnea index (AHI, events/h) from baseline to week 52. Seven key multiplicity-controlled secondary end points included change in sleep apnea-specific hypoxic burden, the Patient-Reported Outcomes Measurement Information System Short Form Sleep-Related Impairment T-score, and high-sensitivity C-reactive protein. A total of 363 patients were randomized in trial 1 (mean age, 48.4 years; BMI, 37.4; AHI, 50.7 events/h; 31.4% female) and 349 patients were randomized in trial 2 (mean age, 51.1 years; BMI, 38.6; AHI, 57.6 events/h; 26.9% female). For the treatment regimen estimand, in trial 1, the mean AHI change was -17.8 for orforglipron compared with -4.5 for placebo (difference, -13.2 [95% CI, -17.7 to -8.7]; P < .001) at 52 weeks. In trial 2, the mean AHI change was -17.3 for orforglipron and -5.3 for placebo (difference, -12.0 [95% CI, -17.1 to -6.9]; P < .001) at 52 weeks. Of 7 key secondary end points, 6 were statistically significant, favoring orforglipron. Gastrointestinal events were the most commonly reported adverse events, occurring in 123 (68.0%) participants randomized to receive orforglipron vs 68 (37.4%) randomized to receive placebo in trial 1 and in 125 (70.6%) participants randomized to receive orforglipron vs 63 (36.6%) randomized to receive placebo in trial 2. These results provide evidence for the potential use of oral orforglipron to improve sleep-disordered breathing in adults with moderate to severe OSA and obesity or overweight. ClinicalTrials.gov Identifier: NCT06649045.

papers.title: Time-dependent efficacy of vitamin D3 against chronic stress-induced behavioral and circadian deficits via the hepatic VDR-clock axis.
papers.abstract: Vitamin D3 (VitD3) is an essential fat-soluble micronutrient that protects against chronic stress-related disorders through its neuroprotective and anti-inflammatory effects. Major depressive disorder is accompanied by circadian rhythm (CR) disruption, and evidence from chrono-nutrition studies suggests that nutrient effects are strongly influenced by administration timing. However, whether VitD3 efficacy against chronic stress depends on intervention timing remains unclear. This study assessed the chrono-nutrition potential of VitD3 in a mouse model of chronic stress. Mice subjected to 4 weeks of chronic unpredictable mild stress (CUMS) received daily VitD3 either in the morning (AM) or evening (PM). VitD3 treatment mitigated CUMS-induced behavioral impairments, neuroinflammation, and neuronal damage in a time-dependent manner, with superior outcomes observed with PM administration. PM administration enhanced anxiety- and depression-like behaviors, hippocampal integrity, TNF-α levels, sleep duration, and serotonin synthesis. Mechanistically, PM administration more effectively restored hepatic Vdr rhythmic oscillation, coupled with re-synchronization of the core clock network. Genetic validation in Caenorhabditis elegans further supported the essential role of VDR in circadian restoration. This study is the first to reveal the time-dependent antidepressant effects of VitD3 and identify the VDR-circadian clock axis as the underlying mechanism. These findings highlight the importance of intervention timing for VitD3 efficacy and support precision nutrition strategies aligned with CR for stress disorders.

papers.title: Clinical features of the postictal state in adults with epilepsy: A cross-sectional survey.
papers.abstract: Persons with epilepsy may experience many postictal symptoms after a seizure, which can significantly impact quality of life. We aimed to determine the frequency, duration, and severity of postictal symptoms to better characterize the postictal period. Our cross-sectional questionnaire was adapted from a prior pediatric postictal survey. Face and content validity were evaluated by epilepsy experts and patients from the Calgary Epilepsy Program (CEP). The survey was pilot tested and modified, consisting of 14 physical, cognitive, and psychiatric postictal signs and symptoms. Consecutive CEP adults who had agreed to participate in research and experienced a seizure in the prior 2 years were approached. CEP clinical data were used to supplement survey data. Frequency of factors alleviating and exacerbating postictal symptoms were examined. Spearman's rho was used to explore associations between survey and CEP registry data with statistical significance at ≤ 0.05. Of 351 patients approached, 313 agreed to participate (89%). Fourteen were lost after consent was obtained, and 15 were excluded (incomplete surveys, missing registry data, not having epilepsy). Of the 298 final participants, 54% were female, mean age was 40 years (SD = 15.6), and 95% (282/298) experienced at least one postictal symptom. The three most frequent postictal symptoms were fatigue, sleepiness, or tiredness (84%), confusion or difficulty thinking clearly (75%), and memory problems (69%). For eight of 14 captured postictal symptoms, the most frequently reported symptom duration was <5 min. Mean postictal symptom burden score was correlated with patient reported quality of life and epilepsy-related disability measures. Sleep or rest, medication, and food or drinks were the most common alleviating factors. Lack of rest or sleep, and stress most often exacerbated postictal symptoms. This work contributes toward a better understanding of the postictal period and informs the development of future interventions to minimize the impact of the postictal period in epilepsy.

papers.title: Evidence of high rates of burnout symptoms in a cohort with cluster headache.
papers.abstract: Cluster headache is a debilitating primary headache disorder. During active bouts, headache attacks occur daily and can last up to 3 h. Besides the excruciating pain, the disorder can greatly impact a patient's mental health, sleep, and life quality. The reoccurring attacks as well as sleep problems may lead to energy depletion and burnout symptoms, which can limit a person's ability to participate in society to the extent they would like to. Our aim was to investigate the extent of burnout symptoms in a Swedish cluster headache cohort using a cross-sectional approach. We further wanted to study if burnout symptoms can be linked to disease status-and if sex, lifestyle factors, or any specific clinical characteristics may be linked to change in burnout symptoms. Between January 2024 and September 2025, the Shirom-Melamed Burnout Questionnaire was sent out via the Research Electronic Data Capture platform to 839 study participants with cluster headache. Global scores from the questionnaire were compared between study participants in active bout and remission. Likewise, the scores were analyzed between participants whose remission period had lasted longer than 5 years (long-term) compared to less than 5 years (short-term). Lifestyle and clinical factors were further analyzed in study participants with high Shirom-Melamed Burnout Questionnaire scores (global score >3.75). The total number of individuals included in the analysis was 373/839 (44.5%). Scores above threshold (>3.75) were recorded in 65.9% (58/88) of study participants in an active bout compared to 37.5% (90/240) in the remission group (odds ratio [OR] = 3.22, 95% confidence interval [CI] = 1.93-5.38; p < 0.001). Participants in short-term remission similarly had a higher percentage of scores above threshold compared to participants in long-term remission (42.0% [73/174] vs. 22.2% [12/54], OR = 2.53, 95% CI = 1.25-5.14; p = 0.009). Participants with burnout scores above 3.75 were more likely to be females (OR = 3.25, 95% CI = 2.04-5.19; pcorrected <0.001) and report sleep deprivation as an attack trigger (OR = 2.24, 95% CI = 1.32-3.82; pcorrected = 0.034). Participants with cluster headache in our Swedish cohort reported higher scores for burnout symptoms, particularly during active bout. For participants in remission, the burnout symptoms score was inversely correlated to the number of years since their last active headache bout. When managing cluster headache in a clinical setting, it should be taken into consideration that this patient group has a substantial risk for developing burnout symptoms both in and out of an active bout. Future studies should evaluate how to best support patients with cluster headache handling exhaustion and promote recovery to improve their quality of life.

papers.title: Risk of obstructive sleep apnea in patients with polycystic ovary syndrome by body mass index: Retrospective cohort study with Korean nationwide population-based cohort.
papers.abstract: Polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS) is a gynecologic endocrine disorder affecting various aspects of women's health. Research examining the association between PCOS, obesity, and obstructive sleep apnea (OSA) in Korean populations remains limited. We assessed OSA risk in Korean with PCOS, considering body mass index (BMI). We conducted a retrospective cohort study using health insurance claims data from the National Health Insurance Service. We selected 33 638 people with PCOS and 98 110 controls with available BMI data. This is a subgroup representing our previous retrospective cohort study, which identified the relationship between PCOS and several mental disorders. Hazard ratios (HR) for PCOS were calculated using Cox proportional hazards regression models. Obese individuals had a higher prevalence of OSA (0.60% in people with PCOS, 0.20% in controls) compared with the non-obese individuals (0.12% in people with PCOS, 0.13% in controls). PCOS (hazard ratio [HR]: 1.483, 95% confidence interval [CI]: 1.029-2.137) and BMI (HR: 1.104, 95% CI: 1.069-1.141) were associated with an increased risk of OSA. Our findings suggest that the risk of OSA is higher in people with PCOS. This research holds significance by indicating that obesity at the time of PCOS diagnosis could serve as a potential predictor for OSA. This study supports international PCOS guidelines that recommend screening and managing OSA.

papers.title: The Clinical Profile and Bedside Clues of Anti-LGI1 Encephalitis Presenting With Isolated Cognitive Impairment: A Multicenter Retrospective Cohort Study.
papers.abstract: A significant subset of anti-LGI1 encephalitis manifests initially with isolated cognitive impairment. Characterizing the clinical profile and bedside clues is critical for timely diagnosis and treatment. This multicenter retrospective cohort study enrolled 43 patients with isolated cognitive impairment during the first 2 weeks of illness. Patients were classified according to their entire disease course into sustained isolated impairment versus evolving neuropsychiatric syndrome. Domain-specific cognitive deficits (assessed using the Montreal Cognitive Assessment [MoCA]), paraclinical findings, and treatment response were systematically evaluated. Median age was 58 years and 67.4% were male. The MoCA revealed delayed recall impairment in 93.0%, with relatively preserved naming. Additional neuropsychiatric symptoms developed in 69.8% of patients, with median latencies as follows: psychiatric symptoms (21 days), FBDS (30 days), and focal seizures (47.5 days). The remaining 30.2% suffered from a sustained isolated cognitive impairment. The sustained-isolation subgroup was younger, had fewer naming deficits, and a similar immunotherapy response. EEG abnormalities (53.9%) and mesial temporal MRI hyperintensities (61.5%) were common in this subgroup. Isolated cognitive impairment frequently evolves into a broader neuropsychiatric syndrome, but a subset remains isolated. Delayed recall impairment with relative naming preservation, together with EEG and MRI findings, constitutes a practical bedside triad prompting early antibody screening and timely immunotherapy.

papers.title: A Pragmatic Approach for Brain-First and Body-First Classification in Parkinson's Disease: Insights from the Personalized Parkinson Project.
papers.abstract: The brain-first versus body-first framework in Parkinson's disease (PD) proposes distinct origins of α-synuclein pathology, resulting in discrete progression patterns. Although this pathophysiological distinction implies different clinical trajectories, feasible criteria to classify subjects in large cohorts are currently lacking. The goal was to develop a pragmatic approach for classifying brain-first and body-first PD clinical subtypes in a large early-PD cohort. We, therefore, explored a pragmatic approach to separating these subtypes based on motor asymmetry, rapid eye movement sleep behavior disorder, and orthostatic hypotension, applied in a large cohort of persons with early PD (disease duration <5 years). Individuals classified as probable brain-first were more often tremor-dominant and showed a trend toward less constipation, after adjusting for disease duration, age and sex. This framework enables subtyping in many existing cohorts, potentially advancing our understanding of PD pathophysiology and facilitating targeted therapies. Validation against gold-standard measures is recommended to refine these criteria further.

papers.title: Heteroatom effects on tricyclic fused aromatic molecules revealed by rotational spectroscopy.
papers.abstract: The gas-phase structures of dibenzothiophene, dibenzofuran, and carbazole provide detailed insights into how heteroatomic substitution changes the structural and electronic characteristics of tricyclic aromatic systems. Here we investigated the molecular properties such as rotational constants and the geometry of the three compounds in a supersonic expansion using high-resolution chirped-pulse Fourier transform microwave (CP-FTMW) spectroscopy in a recently built spectrometer operating in the 2-18 GHz frequency range. Assisted by ab initio (MP2) and density functional theory (B3LYP-D3(BJ)) quantum-chemical calculations, the spectral analysis allowed us to assign the parent species and the heavy-atom isotopologues in natural abundance (13C and either 15N,34S, or 18O) for all three molecules. The isotopic data enabled the determination of the experimental structure through several methods, namely the substitution structure (rs), the vibrational ground-state geometry (r0), the semi-experimental equilibrium structure (rSEe), and the first-order mass-dependent r(1)m structure, through analysis of the changes in the principal moments of inertia induced by single-atom isotopic substitution. The experimental structures of these three heteroatom-containing PAHs are compared with the previously reported fluorene molecule. Finally, we discuss the underlying structural and electronic changes caused by the heteroatoms in the fluorene scaffold.

papers.title: Independent and joint associations of physical activity, sedentary behavior, and sleep with vitamin D status in US adults: a cross-sectional NHANES study.
papers.abstract: Emerging evidence links movement behaviors to vitamin D status. This study investigated associations between physical activity (PA), sedentary behavior (SB), and sleep with vitamin D status and explored sex differences in these relationships. This cross-sectional study included 3195 adults (49.1 ± 17.1 years, 45.5% males) from the 2021-2023 National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey with complete data. Self-reported PA, SB, and sleep duration were assessed. Serum 25-hydroxyvitamin D was measured using high-performance liquid chromatography-tandem mass spectrometry. Generalized linear and logistic regression models were performed. SB was negatively associated with vitamin D levels in the whole sample (β = -0.006; 95% confidence interval [CI]: -0.012, -0.001) and males (β = -0.008; 95% CI: -0.014, -0.002), but not females. Sleep duration was positively associated with vitamin D among males only (β = 0.023; 95% CI: 0.003, 0.043). Meeting both PA and SB guidelines showed the strongest and most consistent association with vitamin D sufficiency, observed across the whole sample (odds ratio [OR] = 2.129; 95% CI: 1.504, 3.012), males (OR = 2.013; 95% CI: 1.021, 3.967), and females (OR = 2.214; 95% CI: 1.360, 3.605). Movement behaviors demonstrate independent and joint associations with vitamin D status in US adults, with modest sex-specific patterns that warrant replication. Combined adherence to PA and SB guidelines was consistently associated with greater odds of vitamin D sufficiency across sexes.

papers.title: Phenotypic and genetically predicted sleep traits in relation to dementia incidence in Swedish twins.
papers.abstract: Sleep and dementia are complex phenotypes shaped by genetic and environmental factors, but the genetic contribution of sleep to dementia risk remains unclear. This study examined associations of both phenotypic and genetically predicted sleep traits and their interaction with dementia risk. Data were drawn from the Screening Across the Lifespan Twin study (1998 to 2002) within the Swedish Twin Registry. Phenotypic sleep traits included sleep duration, insomnia, snoring, daytime sleepiness, chronotype, daytime napping, and a composite sleep score. Corresponding polygenic scores (PGSs) were derived from publicly available genome-wide association study summary statistics. Dementia diagnosis was obtained from national registers. Cox proportional hazards models estimated risk, excluding cases diagnosed within 10 years of baseline to reduce reverse causation. Among 13,087 individuals (mean age 70.27; 1541 dementia diagnosis cases), longer sleep duration (hazard ratio [HR] 0.93; 95% confidence interval [CI]: 0.86 to 1.00; p = 0.04) was associated with lower dementia risk over 13.42 years in models adjusted for sociodemographic and lifestyle behavioral factors. In within-pair analyses, this association was attenuated. Among 16,164 genotyped individuals (mean age 55.32; 559 cases), a one-standard deviation higher PGS for daytime napping (HR 1.12; 95% CI: 1.01 to 1.23; p = 0.03) was associated with higher dementia risk over 16.01 years. In 3133 individuals with both data types (mean age 66.79 years; 377 cases), this association persisted independently of phenotypic napping (HR 1.17; 95% CI: 1.03 to 1.33; p = 0.02), with no interaction observed. Genetic liability to daytime napping in midlife may reflect a distinct vulnerability for dementia, whereas napping in late-life may serve a compensatory or restorative function.

papers.title: Women with the FMR1 premutation: a within-family observational sibling study.
papers.abstract: Understanding the relative risk of the fragile X messenger ribonucleoprotein 1 (FMR1) premutation (PM) versus the risk of the PM and parenting a child with fragile X syndrome (FXS) is critical for PM carriers, their families and clinicians. For this study, we compared women with the PM with their biological sisters; some sisters also had the PM and some had normal-range cytosine-guanine-guanine (CGG) repeats. The sisters were further differentiated by whether they had a child with FXS. This study of 67 women from 30 families used multilevel modelling to probe the effects of the PM with or without parenting a child with FXS, with strong control for family-of-origin factors and background genetics. Controlling for the false discovery rate, we found that mothers with the PM who had children with FXS were similar to their sisters who had the PM but did not have a child with FXS in health, sleep, social relationships, depressive symptoms and executive functioning, differing only in anxiety and stress. However, there were many differences when mothers with the PM who had children with FXS were compared with their sisters with normal-range CGGs, including greater fragile X-associated tremor/ataxia syndrome-type, depressive and anxiety symptoms, poorer sleep, greater negative support and greater stress. In this study, the effect of the PM was stronger than the effect of parenting a child with FXS. Thus, the PM phenotype should not be primarily attributed to the effect of parenting a child with FXS. Additionally, by comparing mothers who had the PM and children with FXS with their sisters without the PM, the findings confirmed the effect of this dual vulnerability and here the vulnerability emerged even with strong familial controls.

papers.title: Avermectin poisoning with panic-like symptoms: a case series.
papers.abstract: High doses of avermectin, a macrolide derived from Streptomyces avermitilis, can cause coma, delirium, respiratory failure, hypotension, and acidosis. However, certain adverse toxicological effects and psychological implications remain unrecognized in patients undergoing parasuicide. Case 1: A 54-year-old man ingested approximately 500 mL avermectin benzylate. He was found to be somnolent 45 min later. Subsequently, the patient became unconscious with respiratory failure, hypotension, and acidosis (lactate, 16.2 mmol/L). Gastric lavage, mechanical ventilation, hemoperfusion, hemofiltration, and symptomatic treatments were administered. Three days after ingestion, the patient's primary symptoms were delirium and myoclonus, with a blood avermectin level of 110.06 μg/L. Thereafter, intermittent shaking, limb flexion, and muscle rigidity persisted. Thirteen days after ingestion, brain magnetic resonance imaging was unremarkable. Electroencephalography revealed no epileptiform discharges. After psychiatric evaluation, the patient was assessed as having panic-like symptoms, and his symptoms improved significantly with specialized treatment. Case 2: A 33-year-old man was injected with approximately 5 mL of 1% avermectin in his left forearm. Two days later, he reported significant pain and swelling along with intermittent palpitations, dizziness, and limb tremors consistent with panic-like symptoms. His blood avermectin level was 0.02 μg/mL. After 7 days of treatment, the swelling subsided, and the panic-like symptoms resolved. Avermectin poisoning causes significant toxic effects, including respiratory failure, hypotension, acidosis, coma, and delirium. Intramuscular injections may result in localized swelling. Parasuicide patients may also present with panic-like symptoms requiring careful differential diagnosis.

papers.title: Rheumatoid Arthritis and Sleep Disturbances: A Narrative Review of Bidirectional Mechanisms.
papers.abstract: Rheumatoid arthritis (RA) is a systemic autoimmune disease in which sleep disturbances are common and closely linked to pain, fatigue, mood symptoms, physical dysfunction, and disease activity. This narrative review synthesizes clinical and mechanistic evidence for a bidirectional relationship between RA and impaired sleep while distinguishing diagnosed sleep disorders from transdiagnostic sleep symptoms. RA-related inflammation, pain, stiffness, and psychological comorbidity may impair sleep through peripheral-to-central inflammatory signaling, altered monoamine metabolism, circadian disruption, hypothalamic-pituitary-adrenal axis dysfunction, autonomic hyperarousal, and central sensitization. Conversely, insufficient or fragmented sleep may disrupt immune and circadian homeostasis, amplify pro-inflammatory signaling and pain sensitivity, and thereby worsen RA symptoms and possibly disease activity. However, much of the available evidence is cross-sectional, based on patient-reported sleep, or derived from small treatment studies, so direct causality and the independent contribution of individual pathways remain uncertain. Evidence from cytokine-blocking and sleep-directed interventions suggests potential benefit, but improvements may be mediated through changes in pain, fatigue, mood, and inflammatory activity. Age, sex, adiposity, medications, depression, anxiety, and sleep-disorder phenotype further modify these associations. Clinically, RA care should distinguish insomnia, obstructive sleep apnea, restless legs syndrome, circadian problems, and non-diagnostic sleep symptoms, then combine optimized RA and pain management with disorder-specific sleep treatment. Longitudinal multimodal cohorts and adequately powered trials using both patient-reported and objective sleep outcomes are priorities.

papers.title: Health Information Literacy Moderates the Associations of Perceived Social Support with Insomnia and Infertility Psychological Distress in Women Undergoing Assisted Reproductive Technology: A Cross-Sectional Study.
papers.abstract: Psychological distress is common among women undergoing assisted reproductive technology (ART). Perceived social support, insomnia, and health information literacy may be interrelated with psychological distress during fertility treatment, but their conditional relationships remain insufficiently understood. This study examined the indirect association between perceived social support and infertility psychological distress through insomnia and whether health information literacy moderated the associations among perceived social support, insomnia, and IPD. A cross-sectional survey was conducted from March to August 2024, enrolling 1007 women undergoing ART at two tertiary hospitals in Wuhan, China. Standardized instruments, including the Perceived Social Support Scale (PSS), the Insomnia Severity Index (ISI), the Everyday Health Information Literacy (HIL) questionnaire, and the Infertility Psychological Distress (IPD) Scale, were utilized for data collection. Mediation and moderated mediation analyses were conducted using PROCESS Models 4 and 59 with 5000 bootstrap samples. Seven prespecified sociodemographic and clinical covariates were included in the analyses. PSS was negatively associated with IPD (B = -0.364, p < 0.001) and ISI (B = -0.094, p < 0.001). A significant indirect association between PSS and IPD through ISI was observed (indirect effect = -0.132, 95% bootstrap CI [-0.175, -0.094]). HIL significantly moderated the associations between PSS and ISI (B = -0.008, p < 0.001), between PSS and IPD (B = -0.029, p < 0.001), and between ISI and IPD (B = -0.071, p = 0.003). At higher levels of HIL, the negative associations of PSS with ISI and IPD were stronger, whereas the positive association between ISI and IPD was weaker. In this cross-sectional study, PSS was indirectly associated with IPD through ISI, and HIL modified the associations among PSS, ISI, and IPD. These findings suggest that social support, sleep problems, and HIL may be usefully considered together in psychosocial assessment during ART. Longitudinal and intervention studies are needed to determine the temporal and causal relationships among these factors.

papers.title: Lifestyle-Based Interventions for Major Depressive Disorder and Their Role Alongside Antidepressant Treatment: A Systematic Review.
papers.abstract: Major depressive disorder (MDD) remains disabling despite effective pharmacotherapy, and many patients experience an incomplete response or residual symptoms. This systematic review evaluated randomized trials of structured exercise or mind-body exercise, sleep/circadian and bright-light interventions, whole-diet interventions, and multicomponent lifestyle programs delivered alongside antidepressant treatment in adults with current MDD. PubMed, Europe PMC, and ClinicalTrials.gov were searched from inception through September 15, 2026, with supplementary citation searching of eligible reports and relevant reviews. The electronic searches identified 1,310 records. After the removal of 333 duplicate bibliographic records and one non-usable record, 976 records underwent screening. Thirty-eight reports were assessed at full text. Following eligibility assessment and final verification, 26 eligible reports remained from the original search, and eight additional eligible reports were identified through supplementary citation searching. The final review included 34 reports representing 29 independent randomized studies. Risk of bias was assessed using the Cochrane Risk of Bias 2 (RoB 2) tool, certainty of evidence was evaluated using Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development and Evaluation (GRADE), and results were synthesized without meta-analysis because substantial clinical and methodological heterogeneity made a pooled estimate inappropriate. Structured exercise showed the most consistent favorable signal, although effects were generally smaller or less certain in trials using active comparators. Sleep/circadian and bright-light interventions showed possible short-term benefits in selected studies, but findings varied by intervention, comparator, and assessment time, and sustained benefits were inconsistent. Evidence for multicomponent lifestyle programs was sparse, and no eligible randomized trial evaluated a whole-diet intervention alone as an adjunct to antidepressant treatment. Overall certainty of the evidence was low to very low because of risk of bias, inconsistency, and imprecision. Lifestyle-based interventions may provide additional benefit as adjuncts to antidepressant treatment, particularly structured exercise and selected sleep/circadian interventions; however, the magnitude and durability of benefit remain uncertain. Substitution of lifestyle interventions for antidepressant medication was not evaluated in this review.

papers.title: The use of wearable devices in the community to detect symptom severity and relapse of psychosis: A systematic review.
papers.abstract: Psychosis is a debilitating illness, marked by frequent relapses that are difficult to manage. Community mental health care can be reactive and inconsistent, but wearable devices offer the potential to monitor clinical status using biometric data (e.g. sleep-wake cycle, physical activity, heart rate). This study evaluates the feasibility of using wearable devices and examines if they can detect early warning signs of clinical deterioration and relapse in people with psychosis in the community setting. A systematic review following Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses guidelines, consisting of 18- to 65-year-olds living in the community with psychosis. Only studies using a wearable device (research- or consumer-grade) with direct skin contact measuring biometric markers (e.g. actigraphy, electrodermal activity, heart rate variability) were included. Twenty-seven studies met the inclusion criteria, with 18 unique studies. Schizophrenia spectrum disorders were the predominant diagnoses, and the Positive and Negative Syndrome Scale was the most used clinical outcome measure. Most studies (12/18) were short-term (<28 days). Physical activity via actigraphy (n = 18) was most commonly examined, followed by sleep-wake cycle (n = 16) and heart rate (n = 13), with some integrating smartphone-based ecological momentary assessment (n = 8). Three unique studies attempted to detect relapse by combining wearable data with clinical data. Overall, most studies carried a serious risk of bias, primarily due to confounding and selective reporting. The use of wearable devices in community settings is feasible for monitoring the severity of psychotic symptoms and may detect relapse, though findings are limited by heterogeneity in wearable and clinical measures and study design.

papers.title: When SOREMPs Meet Episodic Hypersomnia: REM Dysregulation as a Trait or State in Kleine-Levin Syndrome.
papers.abstract: REM dysregulation in Kleine-Levin syndrome may reflect a trait, an episode-dependent state, or profound hypersomnolence; SOREMPs should therefore be interpreted in the context of the longitudinal clinical phenotype.

papers.title: Clinical performance and applicability of prediction models using wearable-derived physiologic signals to anticipate migraine or headache attacks: A systematic review.
papers.abstract: This study evaluated the performance, risk of bias, and clinical applicability of prediction models using wearable-derived or ambulatory physiologic signals to anticipate short-term migraine or headache outcomes in adults. A migraine or headache forecast can support self-management only when it is accurate, calibrated, actionable, and associated with an acceptable false-alarm burden. Wearable devices estimate autonomic, activity, and sleep-related features from surrogate signals, but their clinical readiness has not been systematically evaluated. We reviewed prediction-model studies using objective wearable or ambulatory physiologic signals to anticipate migraine or headache outcomes in adults. PubMed/MEDLINE, Scopus, and Web of Science Core Collection were searched from inception to May 18, 2026. Reporting was structured according to Transparent Reporting of a Multivariable Prediction Model for Individual Prognosis or Diagnosis-Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses, with Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses 2020 used for study selection. We used Prediction Model Risk of Bias Assessment Tool/Prediction Model Risk of Bias Assessment Tool +artificial intelligence-compatible criteria and a task-specific narrative synthesis. Eight studies were included. Tasks were near-onset detection (20-40 min), night-to-next-day forecasting, and multi-day forecasting. Among comparable models, area under the receiver operating characteristic curve ranged from 0.62 to 0.84. In the largest study (146 adults; 21,550 prediction days), area under the receiver operating characteristic curve was 0.84 (95% confidence interval, 0.82-0.85) for next-day moderate-to-severe headache and 0.76 (95% confidence interval, 0.74-0.77) for a 3-day horizon. Five studies had high analysis-domain risk of bias and three had some concerns. No study reported external validation; calibration was reported once. Wearable-based prediction models remain early proof-of-concept studies, not clinically validated alert systems. Their reported discrimination may partly reflect between-person differences in headache frequency rather than within-person forecasting. External validation, calibration, threshold-specific alert burden, and evidence that acting on forecasts improves outcomes are needed before clinical use.

papers.title: BiXCA-DualFormer: A time-frequency fusion model for epileptic seizure prediction.
papers.abstract: Epileptic seizure prediction based on electroencephalography (EEG) is important for developing early-warning technologies and improving patient safety. However, reliable prediction remains challenging because preictal EEG changes are subtle and non-stationary, with discriminative information distributed across both temporal and spectral domains. The purpose of this study is to develop a seizure prediction framework that can jointly model complementary temporal and spectral EEG information and capture their interactions. To this end, we propose BiXCA-DualFormer, a dual-branch time-frequency fusion model. Raw EEG signals and short-time Fourier transform representations are processed through separate temporal and spectral branches to extract complementary waveform and frequency-domain features. The main methodological contribution of the proposed model is the introduction of bidirectional cross-attention to explicitly exchange information between the two branches, followed by a Transformer encoder and learnable query pooling for global dependency modeling and feature aggregation. Experiments on the CHB-MIT dataset showed that the proposed model achieved 95.29% accuracy, 96.40% sensitivity, 95.05% specificity, and a false positive rate of 0.0495. Ablation analysis indicated that time-frequency interaction and global contextual modeling improved sensitivity and discriminative performance. These results suggest that BiXCA-DualFormer provides an effective end-to-end biomedical signal processing framework for EEG-based seizure prediction.

papers.title: Absence of Markers of Inflammation in Blood and Cerebrospinal Fluid in Routine Analysis of Adult and Paediatric Narcolepsy Type 1.
papers.abstract: Narcolepsy Type 1 (NT1) is caused by selective loss of hypocretin-producing hypothalamic neurons, likely mediated by immune mechanisms in genetically predisposed individuals. Evidence of inflammation in routine blood and cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) analyses remains inconsistent. We investigated whether standard plasma and CSF inflammatory markers differ between NT1 at variable latency from disease onset and other central disorders of hypersomnolence (CDH, non-NT1). Consecutive untreated patients evaluated for suspected CDH at a tertiary sleep centre between January 2022 and December 2024 underwent standardized diagnostic assessment including lumbar puncture. Routine blood markers (white blood cell count, neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio [NLR], C-reactive protein, erythrocyte sedimentation rate) and CSF parameters (cell count, protein, glucose, CSF/serum albumin quotient, IgG index, oligoclonal bands) were compared between NT1 and non-NT1 patients. Sensitivity analyses stratified patients by age group, disease duration and HLA-DQB1*06:02 status. We recruited 166 patients with NT1 and 136 with non-NT1 CDH. NT1 patients were younger and had higher body mass index. No significant differences in blood or CSF assay (including NLR, oligoclonal bands, blood-brain barrier permeability, or intrathecal IgG synthesis) were detected after adjustment for age and body mass index. Findings were consistent in paediatric and adult subgroups and in HLA-DQB1*06:02-positive patients. No differences in blood or CSF assays were associated with disease duration (< 1 year vs. 1-3 years vs. > 3 years) in NT1. In conclusion, routine plasma and CSF inflammatory markers do not distinguish NT1 from other CDH, even close to disease onset, supporting the need for more sensitive biomarkers to assess inflammation in NT1.

papers.title: The Relationship of Triglyceride/Glucose Index with Disease Severity, Sleep, and Cognitive Functions in Patients with Geriatric Depression: A Comparative Cross-Sectional Study with Healthy Controls.
papers.abstract: This cross-sectional study investigated the association between the TyG index - a peripheral insulin resistance marker - and depression status, clinical severity, sleep quality, and cognitive functions in drug-naïve older adults compared to healthy controls. Older adults aged 60-74 (mean: 66.2 ± 3.8, range: 60-74; 65.5% depressed) comprising 76 patients with MDD and 40 controls were evaluated using GDS-15, ISI, and SMMSE. Assessor-blinded to the clinical psychiatric status of the participants. The TyG index was significantly higher in patients than controls. Within the depressed cohort (n = 76), the TyG index correlated significantly with depression severity (r = 0.401, p < .001), but its cross-sectional associations with cognitive function (p = .110) and insomnia severity (p = .163) were non-significant. In multivariate logistic regression adjusted for age, sex, education, BMI, and comorbidities, the TyG index remained independently associated with higher odds of depression status (Exp(B)=24.935, p < .001). Exploratory ROC analysis revealed that a tentative cutoff of >8.78 discriminated depressed individuals with 63.16% sensitivity and 95.00% specificity (AUC = 0.804, p < .001). The TyG index is cross-sectionallyassociated with depression status and clinical severity in drug-naïveolder adults, independent of BMI. The TyG index represents a cost-effective, noninvasive exploratory metabolic biomarker that may complement clinical screenings in late-life psychiatry.

papers.title: Effects of Group-Based CBT/ERP and ACT on Emotion Dysregulation, Sleep, Anxiety Sensitivity and Psychological Flexibility in Adults With OCD.
papers.abstract: Cognitive behavioural therapy with exposure and response prevention (CBT/ERP) is the recommended first-line psychological treatment for obsessive-compulsive disorder (OCD). Acceptance and commitment therapy (ACT) has emerged as a promising alternative, yet treatment comparisons have primarily focused on symptom severity and even less is known about their effects on other domains. We examined the effect of group-based ACT and CBT/ERP on emotion regulation, anxiety sensitivity, insomnia and psychological flexibility in adults with OCD. 176 adults with OCD were randomized to CBT/ERP or ACT and assessed with the Difficulties in Emotion Regulation Scale (DERS), Sleep Condition Indicator (SCI), Anxiety Sensitivity Index-Revised (ASI-R) and Acceptance and Action Questionnaire for Obsessions and Compulsions (AAQ-OC) at baseline, post-treatment, 6-month and 12-month follow-up and analysed with Mixed-Model Repeated Measures (MMRM). Both treatments showed similar improvements in the four domains across timepoints. In line with our hypotheses, our results indicated that ACT may be non-inferior to CBT/ERP for all secondary outcomes. However, as the trial was powered for the primary outcome (symptom severity) rather than for these secondary measures, our findings should be interpreted as suggestive. Nonetheless, these findings add to the growing evidence that ACT may be considered a viable treatment for OCD.

papers.title: Community-Based Physiotherapy Models and Neurological Trajectories in Infants at High Risk of Cerebral Palsy in Rural Tanzania: A Retrospective Routine-Care Study.
papers.abstract: Cerebral palsy (CP) refers to a group of motor impairments resulting from nonprogressive brain malformations or injuries that occur early in development. Limited access to rehabilitation services in low- and middle-income countries poses substantial challenges. This study aimed to describe the clinical and sociodemographic characteristics of children treated at a rural rehabilitation centre in Tanzania and to evaluate their neurological trajectories across three physiotherapy models. A retrospective longitudinal review (April to September 2025) analysed 126 medical records of children aged 3-24 months who underwent the Hammersmith Infant Neurological Examination (HINE) at the beginning of the intervention and after approximately 3 months of care. Participants were categorized into the hope intensive programme (HPP; 40 h/month), early intervention programme (EIP; 16 h/4 months) or conventional physiotherapy programme (CPP; 16 h/4 months). Neurological function improved across all groups, with substantial raw neurological development gains reflected in the mean HINE scores, which increased from 41.6 to 55.3. Postintervention, the odds of infants remaining in the lowest HINE score range decreased significantly (OR: 0.07). The HPP group showed the fastest developmental progression. The study also supports the feasibility of using the Kiswahili-translated HINE as an excellent low-cost, responsive and context-appropriate tool for longitudinal tracking and clinical monitoring. Structured neurorehabilitation, particularly intensive intervention, was associated with significant raw neurological progression in this low-resource setting, highlighting the utility of the HINE for objective longitudinal surveillance.

papers.title: Effectiveness of Rotating Versus Fixed Three-Section Watchkeeping Schedules on Crews' Well-Being, Cognitive Performance, Sleep and Salivary Cortisol in the Navy.
papers.abstract: When 24 h-work needs to be distributed among crew members on ships, on-watch duty times can be either stable over time or can vary on a regular basis. Research suggests that adaptation to permanent night shift might be less disruptive to humans' innate circadian rhythms than rotating schedules when external and social influences are minimized, such as when working on ships. Since the research on the question of rotation in the design of watchkeeping schedules is still not conclusively answered, the present research investigated the effects of a fixed and a daily rotating three-section watchkeeping schedule on crew members' vigilance performance, well-being, salivary cortisol and sleep quantity and continuity in five underways on board a German frigate. Results revealed better vigilance performance, less acute disruptions in salivary cortisol and less subjective sleepiness in the rotating watchkeeping schedule, especially for the night watch (watch on duty from 00 to 04). In contrast, sleep continuity was better in the fixed watchkeeping schedule. In sum, results favour rotating three-section watchkeeping schedules for cognitive functioning and well-being, but also suggest fixed three-section watchkeeping schedules are more suitable to maintain restorative sleep.

papers.title: Associations of the Low Arousal Threshold With Arrhythmia Burden and Heart Rate Variability in Obstructive Sleep Apnea Using Polysomnography With 24-h Holter Electrocardiography.
papers.abstract: Obstructive sleep apnea (OSA) is a widespread condition that increases the risk of arrhythmias. Recently, the role of specific OSA phenotypes, including the low respiratory arousal threshold (ArTH) phenotype, has been largely explored. This study aimed to assess whether the estimated low ArTH in patients with obstructive sleep apnea is significantly associated with arrhythmia burden and alterations in heart rate variability (HRV). Data from adults who underwent full-night video-polysomnography (vPSG) with 24-h 12-lead Holter electrocardiography (ECG) were included. ArTH was estimated noninvasively using the Edwards method. Arrhythmias were scored and counted. HRV was quantified in time, geometric, and frequency domains using ECG across a predefined circadian schedule. The analysis included 166 participants; 134 were classified as low ArTH, and 32 as high ArTH. The low ArTH group had a lower supraventricular arrhythmia burden, including fewer supraventricular premature contractions (SVPC), fewer SVPC pairs, and fewer supraventricular tachycardia (SVT) episodes than the high ArTH group. Daytime HRV differed between the groups, with higher RMSSD in low ArTH and higher LF power. In multivariable analyses, low ArTH remained associated with SVPC and SVPC pairs. Differences in HRV parameters were limited and were largely attenuated after adjustment for clinical confounders. The results suggest the potential importance of the ArTH phenotype as an independent indicator of arrhythmia in patients with OSA. However, the results should be interpreted as exploratory and hypothesis gathering. Further, prospective studies are needed to assess the utility of ArTH in risk stratification.

papers.title: Plasma-derived hyperhomocysteinemia, PGAM5, and oligomeric α-synuclein as a biomarker panel for idiopathic Parkinson's disease.
papers.abstract: This study aimed to assess a novel panel of plasma biomarkers, comprising homocysteine (HCY), phosphoglycerate mutase 5 (PGAM5), and oligomeric α-synuclein, for the diagnosis of Parkinson's disease (PD) and to investigate the mechanistic interactions among these biomarkers. In this cross-sectional study, serum HCY was measured in all 150 patients with PD and 113 healthy controls (HCs), whereas plasma PGAM5 and oligomeric α-synuclein were assayed in subsets (80 PD/78 HC and 67 PD/89 HC, respectively). The diagnostic associated risk factors, and interrelationships of these biomarkers were analyzed using receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve analysis, multivariable logistic regression, and mediation analysis, respectively. Additionally, a diagnostic nomogram was constructed. Plasma levels of HCY, PGAM5, and oligomeric α-synuclein were significantly elevated in individuals with PD (all P < 0.001). The combined biomarker panel yielded an area under the curve (AUC) of 0.89 for PD diagnosis, which increased to 0.93 when integrated with the rapid eye movement sleep behavior disorder (RBD) questionnaire score. HCY was an independent risk factor for PD and was associated with male sex, older age, hypertension, longer disease duration, and more severe motor/cognitive deficits (all P < 0.01). Oligomeric α-synuclein mediated 25.72% of the association between HCY and PD (P < 0.001). This study validates a high-performance plasma biomarker panel for PD, identifies HCY as a risk factor for severe disease progression, and provides clinical evidence that oligomeric α-synuclein mediates the neurotoxic effect of HCY, highlighting a promising therapeutic target.

papers.title: Differential expression of circadian clock genes and proteins in gingival tissues from patients with stage III grade B periodontitis: a cross-sectional study.
papers.abstract: This study tested the hypothesis that gingival circadian clock gene and protein expressions differ among periodontal health, gingivitis, and stage III grade B periodontitis. Sixty systemically healthy, non-smoking individuals with regular sleep schedules, assessed by the Munich Chronotype Questionnaire, were classified as periodontally healthy (n = 20), gingivitis (n = 20), or stage III grade B periodontitis (n = 20). Gingival biopsies were obtained at a single time point (09:00 to 11:00). Clock gene and protein expressions were analyzed using RT-qPCR and Western blotting. Inflammatory mediators were quantified by RT-qPCR, and IL-1β and IL-6 protein levels were measured by ELISA. Age, sex distribution, sleep duration, and chronotype scores were comparable among groups (p > 0.05). In periodontitis, CLOCK and Per3 were higher, and CRY1, CRY2, and Rev-Erb-β were lower at both gene and protein levels (p < 0.05). Per1 and Per2 were lower at the gene level, whereas Per1 protein did not differ and Per2 protein was lower in both diseased groups (p < 0.05). BMAL1 did not differ at either level, and ROR-α gene expression did not differ (p > 0.05). In pooled exploratory analyses, proinflammatory mediators correlated positively with CLOCK and Per3 and negatively with CRY1, CRY2, Per1, Per2, and Rev-Erb-β, which in turn correlated positively with OPG (FDR-adjusted p < 0.05). RANKL was higher and OPG lower in periodontitis (p < 0.05). Clock gene expressions were also correlated with clinical periodontal parameters. Gingival tissues affected by stage III grade B periodontitis showed differential clock gene and protein expression. Because measurements were obtained at a single time point, these findings indicate differential expression rather than disrupted circadian clock function.

papers.title: Live brain biopsy during CSF shunt surgery for precision diagnostics and multi-omic research.
papers.abstract: Diagnostic testing and neurosurgical management involving CSF shunting in patients with idiopathic normal pressure hydrocephalus (iNPH) offers a unique, ethically sustainable opportunity to study the aging human brain. The common co-occurrence of neurodegenerative pathologies such as amyloid-β plaques and neurofibrillary tau tangles (NFT) provides a valuable window for research into the Alzheimer's disease-related mechanisms. Interindividual variability among iNPH patients enables investigation and validation of biomarkers and molecular mechanisms, opening possibilities for new treatments. In vitro techniques and culturing methods for living brain tissue expand the utility of samples for electrophysiological studies, drug testing, and examining genetic risk variants. Careful sectioning and processing are essential for high-quality samples with intact cells for functional analysis. A rigorous pipeline is also needed for preserving samples for transcriptomic, proteomic, and structural analyses, with emphasis on RNA integrity and tissue architecture for single-cell sequencing and spatial analysis. Here, we review the use of small cortical brain biopsies in neurodegenerative diseases research and diagnostics. Furthermore, we share our team's experience in acquiring and preserving living brain samples during iNPH CSF shunt surgeries, along with our protocols for resection, use, and preservation of biopsies for preclinical research. We highlight the potential of living human tissue for neuroscience, early neurodegenerative disease diagnosis, and targeted therapies.

papers.title: URBANOME: an exposome-based framework linking urban interventions to molecular, health, and policy-relevant outcomes.
papers.abstract: Urban environments expose residents to multiple simultaneous stressors that often act synergistically (e.g., air pollution and extreme heat amplifying cardiovascular and respiratory risks), contributing to a substantial public health burden. Environmental factors account for an estimated 13% of all deaths in the European Union, with ambient air pollution alone responsible for approximately 400,000 premature deaths per year. Most of this burden is mediated through chronic non-communicable diseases, including cardiovascular disease, stroke, cancer, respiratory disease, and mental health outcomes. Because these conditions are shaped by interacting environmental, social, and lifestyle determinants, traditional single-hazard approaches are insufficient, motivating adoption of an exposome paradigm. This paper presents the URBANOME methodological framework, an integrated exposome-based architecture for evaluating urban interventions across external exposures, internal biological responses, functional health outcomes, and policy-relevant indicators, and reports illustrative pilot findings from its first multi-site implementation. In a four-year Horizon 2020 study across nine European cities (Aarhus, Aberdeen, Athens, Ljubljana, Madrid, Milan, Montpellier, Stuttgart, and Thessaloniki), URBANOME implemented an integrated exposome framework through Urban Living Labs (ULLs). Co-created interventions (combining active mobility, urban greening, and traffic calming) were evaluated using a before-after design. Methods included ambient and personal exposure monitoring (wearable sensors, smartphone applications), agent-based population exposure modeling, validated health and well-being questionnaires, objective clinical measures (spirometry, blood pressure, heart rate variability), and multi-omics analyses (untargeted metabolomics and transcriptomics) on biological samples. A cost-benefit analysis quantified the economic return of interventions. The framework was successfully implemented across the nine ULLs, although intervention type, comparator availability, sample size, and follow-up duration varied by site (Table 1). Across paired participants, self-reported air-pollution annoyance and sleep-related breathing problems decreased between baseline and follow-up assessments, and pollution-related differences in forced vital capacity (FVC) were attenuated in higher-exposure neighbourhoods. In an exploratory pilot omics sub-cohort with paired pre/post samples, a four-metabolite panel (L-tyrosine, ascorbic acid, choline, coenzyme Q10) showed apparent perfect internal separation of pre- and post-intervention samples (apparent area under the receiver operating characteristic curve, AUROC ≈ 1.0); given the small sample size and absence of an independent held-out validation set, this result is preliminary and likely overoptimistic, and must be interpreted as a hypothesis-generating finding requiring external validation. Exploratory exposome-lifestyle analyses suggested that co-exposure to poor diet and higher pollution was associated with greater oxidative-stress-related metabolic signals, while combined healthy environments and lifestyles were associated with anti-inflammatory metabolite profiles. An exploratory cost-benefit analysis, based on value-transfer assumptions and standard health-economic unit costs, estimated benefit-cost ratios in the range of approximately €19-€143 per €1 invested across heterogeneous interventions; this range reflects substantial between-site variability and the assumptions detailed in the Methods, and should be interpreted as illustrative rather than as a precise return-on-investment estimate. This paper presents the URBANOME exposome-based evaluation framework and reports illustrative pilot findings from its multi-site implementation. The framework is feasible to deploy across heterogeneous European urban contexts and links external exposure assessment, internal biological profiling, functional health outcomes, and economic appraisal within a single architecture. Observed pre/post changes in self-reported, functional, and molecular endpoints are consistent with potentially beneficial responses to bundled urban interventions, but should be considered preliminary given the heterogeneous before-after design, variable comparator availability, small omics sub-cohorts, and short follow-up. External validation of the candidate biomarker panel and replication in independent settings are required before the framework's outputs can support firm conclusions about intervention effectiveness or cost-effectiveness.

papers.title: Effects of developmental care in neonatal intensive care units on preterm infant outcomes: an umbrella review.
papers.abstract: To synthesize evidence on the effectiveness of developmental care interventions in the NICU on neurodevelopmental outcomes of preterm infants. This umbrella review was conducted in accordance with the Joanna Briggs Institute methodology and reported following the PRISMA guidelines. The Cochrane Library, PubMed, Scopus, PsycINFO, and Web of Science were searched from inception to January 2026. Eligible studies were systematic reviews evaluating the effects of developmental care interventions on neurodevelopmental outcomes in preterm infants. Outcomes included cognitive, motor, behavioral, and socio-emotional domains. Methodological quality was assessed using the AMSTAR 2 tool and overlap among the included reviews was quantified using the Corrected Covered Area (CCA). Twenty-eight systematic reviews were included. Four reviews were rated as high confidence, seven as low, and seventeen as critically low. Developmental care interventions generally improved neurobehavioral organization, cognitive and motor development, sleep, feeding behavior, and parental outcomes. Kangaroo Mother Care and family-centered care showed the most consistent benefits. However, evidence for effects beyond 24 months corrected age was inconsistent. Considerable heterogeneity existed across interventions, outcomes, and follow-up periods. Developmental care interventions appear to improve short-term neurodevelopmental outcomes in preterm infants. However, confidence in the evidence is limited by methodological weaknesses and inconsistent long-term findings, highlighting the need for high-quality longitudinal research. Any protocol amendments will be registered in PROSPERO (CRD42025641814).

papers.title: Transient HBV entry into cerebrospinal fluid following blood-brain barrier disruption: a case of HSV-2 encephalitis with polymicrobial detection elucidated by serial targeted next-generation sequencing.
papers.abstract: Hepatitis B virus (HBV) is traditionally considered a strictly hepatotropic virus, and its neuroinvasive potential remains controversial. When targeted next-generation sequencing (tNGS) simultaneously detects multiple viruses in the cerebrospinal fluid (CSF), distinguishing the true pathogen from bystander viruses poses a clinical challenge. We report a rare case of herpes simplex virus 2 (HSV-2) encephalitis with concurrent detection of HBV and human gammaherpesvirus 4 (HHV-4) in the CSF, and explore the mechanism of HBV entry into the central nervous system (CNS) through serial tNGS before and after treatment, combined with routine CSF analysis. A 42-year-old male with untreated hepatitis B presented with acute fever, frontal and temporal headache for 10 days, unresponsive to empirical anti-infective therapy. EEG revealed increased theta activity in bilateral frontal regions after hyperventilation, suggesting encephalitis. Initial CSF analysis (Day 1) showed marked pleocytosis (white blood cells 1849 × 106/L) and hemorrhagic appearance (red blood cells 1000 × 106/L), indicating acute blood-brain barrier (BBB) disruption. CSF tNGS detected sequences for HSV-2, HHV-4 and HBV. High level of serum HBV DNA with positive HBsAg confirmed active HBV replication. The patient was treated with acyclovir and tenofovir alafenamide (TAF). Repeat lumbar puncture (LP) on Day 17 demonstrated normalized CSF parameters (red blood cells 0 × 106/L, white blood cells 143 × 106/L) and no viral sequences on tNGS. Serum HBV DNA decreased by approximately 2 log10 on the same day. The patient showed significant clinical improvement. Serial CSF tNGS before and after therapy showed synchronous clearance of three viruses with restored BBB integrity and reduced serum HBV DNA, confirming transient passive HBV entry during HSV-2-induced barrier disruption and creating a false polymicrobial picture. These findings highlight serial tNGS as a valuable tool for validating etiological hypotheses and guiding precision therapy in complex CNS infections.

papers.title: Latent subtypes and gender differences in the comorbidity of depression and sleep disturbances among adolescents: insights from network analysis and latent profile analysis.
papers.abstract: This study aimed to explore potential subtypes, influencing factors, and gender differences in the associations between adolescent depression and sleep disorders. A cross-sectional study was conducted among adolescents utilizing the Center for Epidemiologic Studies Depression Scale and the Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index. Latent profile analysis was employed to classify potential subtypes of comorbidities; multinomial logistic regression was used to explore influencing factors across genders; network analysis was conducted to identify core bridging symptoms that mediate the relationship between depression and sleep disturbances. Multi-class logistic regression identified significant gender differences in the factors influencing comorbid depression and sleep disorders. Key risk factors included alcohol use, abnormal weight, living conditions, family economic status, and parental education, with their effects varying between males and females. Higher education emerged as protective factors for adolescents experiencing high comorbidity. The low subtype exhibited the highest network density, while the moderate subtype displayed the lowest density; the high subtype demonstrated increased density alongside a negative correlation with symptoms. CESD11 (Restless sleep) functioned as a core bridging symptom for both genders and subtypes. In females, the pattern of core bridging symptoms transitioned from a mixed depression-sleep structure to polarized pathways dominated by sleep or depression as severity escalated. Conversely, males maintained a balanced combination of depressive and sleep bridging symptoms across all classes, exhibiting no structural polarization. The comorbidity of depression and sleep disorders in adolescents indicates considerable subtype heterogeneity and distinct gender-specific characteristics. Clinically, targeted stratified interventions can be developed by emphasizing core bridging symptoms, while also integrating subtype classification and gender-based features.

papers.title: Development of a Digital Twin to Analyse Waiting Lists in a Sleep-Disordered Breathing Unit.
papers.abstract: This study developed and validated a digital twin of patient flow and waiting list dynamics in a Sleep-Disordered Breathing Unit, based on a discrete-event simulation (DES) model in the context of growing diagnostic demand mainly driven by obstructive sleep apnoea. The stochastic model, implemented in MATLAB, reproduces six care stages (e-Consultation, face-to-face consultation, overnight pulse oximetry, respiratory polygraphy, polysomnography and follow-up consultation), using operational data from year 2024 for parameterisation and data from year 2025 for correlation and validation. Key performance indicators included mean waiting time and mean queue length per stage, with model fidelity assessed via Mean Absolute Error, Root Mean Squared Error and Relative Percent Difference (RPD), both by stage and globally across the full patient pathway. The model accurately reproduced the aggregate system workload, with a weighted RPD of 3.6% for mean queue length and 34.6% for mean waiting time. Respiratory polygraphy showed the best agreement in terms of service load (RPD 2.7%), whereas the follow-up consultation exhibited the largest discrepancies in waiting times (RPD 73.7%), likely related to prioritisation rules and organisational variability not explicitly modelled. Overall, this digital twin provides an operationally useful representation to support 'what-if' analyses of organisational scenarios aimed at reducing diagnostic delays, representing one of the first validated applications of DES model in a dedicated Sleep-Disordered Breathing Unit and provides a basis for future applications incorporating urgency stratification and prospective analysis.

papers.title: Adaptive Spectral Analysis of Umbilical Venous Doppler Maternal-Fetal Power Ratio for Preeclampsia Risk Assessment.
papers.abstract: To develop and evaluate adaptive spectral analysis for deriving the maternal-fetal power ratio (MFPR) from umbilical venous Doppler recordings and to assess MFPR for subsequent preeclampsia (PEC) risk discrimination across recording durations. We retrospectively analyzed second-trimester umbilical venous Doppler recordings in 2 datasets: 83 short acquisitions (mean, 3.4 seconds) from 46 subjects (15 with subsequent PEC), and 126 long acquisitions (mean, 6.9 seconds) from 66 subjects (30 with subsequent PEC). Power spectra were estimated by discrete Fourier transform, Welch, and Capon estimators with adaptive window selection, diagonal loading, and maternal and fetal heart-rate-guided peak localization. MFPR was defined as the decibel difference between the maternal and fetal spectral-peak powers and averaged across clips for each subject (median, 2 clips per subject in both datasets). Discrimination was assessed using group differences, receiver operating characteristic area under the curve (AUC), and Youden's J . Higher MFPR during the second trimester was associated with subsequent development of PEC. For short recordings, heart-rate-guided adaptive Capon performed best (AUC, 0.84; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.70-0.95). For long recordings, heart-rate-guided Welch performed best (AUC, 0.75; 95% CI, 0.60-0.88). Adaptive window selection reduced performance sensitivity to fixed window length, and diagonal loading stabilized covariance inversion. Umbilical venous Doppler MFPR distinguished pregnancies that later developed PEC. The best-performing spectral-analysis pipeline differed between the short and long acquisition datasets. Prospective validation is needed.
